title: Films that have a message of hope and helps you get through tough times?

commenti.body: So many of the Golden Age films are like that, a few of these are my favorites: Signing in the Rain, It's a Wonderful Life, Mr. Smith Goes to Washington, The Best Years of Our Lives, anything with Charlie Chaplin, The Shop Around the Corner, etc.

Shawshank Redemption is a cliche answer but it might be my favorite movie. It has some sad parts for sure, but the ending always makes me tear up with joy for the characters finally able to just, going to meet their friend again.

What first came to mind is the filmography of Mike Leigh. I wouldn't consider his films to have such thing as a 'happy ending' but more of a quality that is embedded in the form of catharsis. They're deeply humane, often depicting people in the fringes of society who face a plethora of struggles. Despair and joy are intertwined, evoking the bittersweet taste of everyday life. In my view they're quite uplifting as they convey the virtues of perseverance and determination of hanging on even amidst all the hardships. I'd reccommend you to start with Secrets and Lies (1996), then proceed to High Hopes (1988), All or Nothing (2002) and perhaps even Topsy Turvy (1999). My favorite of has to be Naked (1993) and while is considered more pessimistic, it would always enlived the shit out of me!

The Fisher King is a touching movie and every time I see it I feel good at the end. I love that it’s a story of redemption for two very different male protagonists. There is a lot of joy in this film that deals with very serious issues like the violent loss of a loved one, suicide, and mental illness. I enjoy the performances so much, although there is a little sadness I feel watching Robin Williams masterfully bring his character to life because I feel that he identified deeply with the material. There is a true character arc and transformation that we see with Jeff Bridges’s character that is so satisfying to watch imo. 

One of my faves, hands down.
I love Secrets & Lies. I haven’t seen the other Mike Leigh films you’ve mentioned but that one changed my film sensibility for the better. Thank you for sharing!

High Noon (1952) is one of my favorite films that exemplifies the overcoming of obstacles when faced with daunting odds. But my ultimate answer to your question is The Best Years of Our Lives (1946) by William Wyler. It’s an absolute masterpiece and I always describe the movie as a warm hug. It leaves you feeling uplifted and believing that no matter how hard your obstacles have been, you can get through it and the best years of your life are still ahead of you.

Jacobinte Swargarajyam (Jacob's Kingdom of Heaven) - It's a Malayalam-language film from the Southern state of Kerala in India. The movie is based on a true story of a Dubai-based business man and his family - the trials and tribulations they face. A testament to picking oneself up from the dumps and moving forward even when you're down and beaten and see no light at the end of the tunnel.

You might or might not relate to the setting, characters and story, but the theme is central - one of human nature. I guess the movie will be available with English subs on Amazon Prime or other platforms depending on where you're situated.

https://youtu.be/ydHzDHz12fw?si=aTZlq-l0Z3s5OUO0
Johnnie To’s Romancing in thin air and Throw Down. To actually has a lot of very life affirming films. Just don’t check out his rom coms unless you wanna see some real bleak cinema lol.

Maybe this will vary for people but Patterson from Jarmusch spoke to me really powerfully about just kinda getting through each day and finding beauty and value in living. The way it talks about time directly and the repetitions in the film somehow transform what could be seen as monotony into wonder and beauty. It's not like a "cheer you up" kind of film but I found it very joyful in how daily life and creativity are portrayed.

The short answer is: Chef.

The more complicated answer is: 127 hours, Saving Private Ryan, Children of Men, Castaway. Bleak, brutal movies, but where the suffering was ultimately worth it or justified or transformational.
I’m not sure how they fit here but I love Naked, Topsy Turvy, and Mr Turner… need to watch more Mike Leigh.
